execution.ref: AGENT-DOOR-USABILITY-01 (.agent/decisions/2026-10-05-AGENT-DOOR-USABILITY-01.md), branch claude/agent-door-usability; owner request via the Graphite Test executor, findings A1, A2, A5, A6 and A7.
execution.description: Agent-facing door fixes: every new run plan freezes argument-normalisation.v2, the miner MCP door's schema follows the frozen rule and answers a schema refusal with the declared field and a registered correction, new phase-3 sessions record a budget-status rule that drops the unmetered trial line, and a phase-3 unserved-backend refusal lists the served backends.

expected: A tolerance one door gives a model's habit holds on every door and every new plan, a refusal tells the agent which field to fix and how, and the turn status names only budgets the ledger actually meters.
observed: Normalisation v2 was frozen only by Graphite plans, so agent-none and autonomous campaigns still refused a practice "null"; the MCP door's schema refused it before the adapter that would read it, with the schema library's dump; phase-3 sessions were told "0 of 0 research trials left" while their experiments ran on pods; and a phase-3 proposal on an unserved backend learned the served ones only by trying again.
keep: A rule a door reads is frozen by every plan builder, and a test enumerates the builders rather than the one the finding came from.
A published schema that follows a frozen rule is pinned byte for byte under every older rule, so only the new rule's campaigns see the change.
A schema refusal names only fields the server declared and registered text; a value is compared, never repeated.
change: When a door gains a tolerance, check every door in front of it: a stricter schema earlier in the path hides the tolerance behind it.
A refusal for an unserved choice carries the served choices from public contract data, so no attempt is spent learning them.
